policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red or blue); call it the goal cube. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a marker telling you which target to use. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, target_before_button unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): first compute target_before_button from the demonstration as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to target_before_button (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [127, 146]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of target_before_button (it may be hidden), point at target_before_button itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and target_before_button is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on target_before_button: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.

fields.name: target_before_button
fields.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is unknown (first step, demonstration shown), compute it from the demonstration steps: find the first demonstration frame whose fingers read 0% open (the gripper is closing on nothing to press the button; the next frames show it low over the button); look backwards from there for the last frame where the fingers went from ~46% open to ~100% open with height under 0.05 (a release); the cube's position in that frame is the placement point; among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, pick the one nearest that placement point and write its [y, x]. e.g. [126, 145]

fields.name: cube_placed
fields.description: 'no' at the first step and at every step until the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to ~100% while the gripper height is under 0.05 and the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of target_before_button; from that step on write 'yes'. e.g. no
